the best way of using BERT is to fine tune it, but that it can still be improved by adding sentence segmentation.
, for biomedical relation extraction, BERT is a good candidate to improve state-of-the-art performances.

, in our context (biomedical RE), fine tuning with Bbert is better than using BERT in a frozen mode, and adding sentence segmentation is better than not adding it, but we are still far from having a clear understanding of the respective advantages of each of these three elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BERT is a very promising approach for biomedical RE, and that the best way to leverage it depends on each specific task.
BERT is a very promising tool for biomedical RE, but its use in transfer learning is still to be fully explored.
, for biomedical RE, BERT is an interesting architecture, but it needs to be fine tuned and to be used in a specific architecture that includes structural information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the task of Biomedical RE, the use of BERT with fine tuning and the addition of sentence level information are two promising directions that deserve further exploration.
the best architecture is highly dependent on the specific task.

the best way to combine the power of BERT and the information provided by structural features is to use a multi-task architecture, where a first task (i.e. a sentence segmentation task) is used to learn the structural features, and a second task (i.e., the RE task) is then used to leverage these features and the context provided by BERT.
